title: Those Who Believe, and Those Who Follow Desires

paragraphs.text: The Prophet was not at the side of the mountain when Allah called Moses. Instead, he was sent as a mercy from his Lord to warn a people who had received no warner before him. Otherwise, if a disaster struck them for their sins, they might complain that no messenger had come. But when the truth did come, they asked why he was not given signs like those of Moses. Yet they had already rejected Moses, calling both messages magic. The Prophet is told to challenge them to bring a scripture from Allah that guides better than both. If they do not respond, they are only following their desires, and no one is more lost than such a person.

Some of those who had received the Scripture before believe in the Quran. When it is recited to them, they say it is the truth from their Lord and that they had already submitted to Him. They will receive their reward twice, because they were patient, they push away evil with good, and they spend from what Allah has given them. When they hear foolish talk, they turn away calmly and say, "Peace be upon you." The Prophet cannot guide whomever he loves; only Allah guides whom He wills.

Some feared that following guidance would get them driven from their land. Yet Allah had given them a safe sanctuary, where fruits of every kind are brought as provision. Many cities proud of their easy lives were destroyed, leaving their homes empty. Allah never destroys cities until a messenger has recited His verses to them, and only when their people are wrongdoers. Everything in this world is temporary enjoyment, while what is with Allah is better and lasts longer. On the Day of Resurrection, He will ask where their false partners are.

hardWords.m: food and things needed for life
